ABSTRACT: Herein, a rhodium-catalyzed highly chemo-, regio-, and
stereo-selective linear cross coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with
readily available 2,3-allenols afforded the synthetically and biologically
versatile 3-alkyn-2(E)-enones/enals. The reaction exhibits a perfect
match of the reactivities for these two classes of compounds since the
well-known self-reacting products of both reactants were not formed.
The reaction enjoys a wide substrate scope under ambient conditions.
Furthermore, the synthetic potentials have been demonstrated by
utilizing this reaction as a pivotal step: a very concise two-step total
synthesis of naturally occurring isotaxifolial D has been achieved; an
efficient synthesis of dehydroacitretin by applying this reaction two times
has also been executed. Through mechanistic studies including D-
labeling experiments, it is proposed that the reaction proceeded via
terminal alkynylmetalation, stereodefined insertion providing a 2-alkynyl π-allylic intermediate, which would undergo C−C single
bond rotation, intramolecular ligand exchange, β−H elimination, and reductive elimination resulting in 1,4-H delivery to afford the
final enynes. The reaction circumvents the use of a stoichiometric amount of base under the catalysis of a single Rh catalyst since
terminal alkynylmetalation is base free, and the catalyst is regenerated by aerobic oxidation in the presence of proton.
KEYWORDS: rhodium catalysis, 1,4-H delivery, enynes synthesis, allenes, alkynes, E-selectivity
■
INTRODUCTION
Transition metal-catalyzed reactions have constantly been
providing highly efficient methodologies for the efficient
formation of covalent bonds. With the fine-tuning of the
ligand structure and metal, the regio-, chemo-, and stereo-
selectivity may be precisely controlled. Terminal alkynes make
up an important class of compounds for such reactions in
organic synthesis. For example, the well-known Sonogashira
coupling of terminal alkynes with 1-alkenyl halides utilizes the
highly reactive C−X bond to form the sp C-sp
2
C bonds under
the co-catalysis of Pd and Cu(I).
1
On the other hand, allenes
have also been becoming one of the most important classes of
organic compounds.
2
Nowadays, the allenation of terminal
alkynes (ATA reaction) has made mono-, di-, and tri-
substituted allenes readily available.
2d
The reactions of
terminal alkynes with allenes have merely been sporadically
studied. Of our interest is the formation of 1-alkynyl π-allylic
metallic species A, which may be converted to enynes A′ and/
or the regioisomeric enynes A″ upon further trapping, although
the formations of non-conjugated alken-4-yn-2-yl metallic
species B and C were also observed (Figure 1a).
3
Beyond
terminal alkynes, decarboxylative alkynylation of allenes with
alkynyl carboxylic acids
4
and transition metal-catalyzed
reactions of haloalkynes with allenes
5
had also been developed.
In 2005, Alcaide and Almendros reported the reaction of
terminal alkynes with 2,3-allenols formed π-allylic metallic
species A1, which readily underwent cyclic etherification to
afford D-type 3-alkynyl-2,5-dihydrofurnans due to the presence
of the nucleophilic OH group (Figure 1b).
6
We report herein
the observation of the Rh-catalyzed highly regio- and stereo-
selective aerobic cross-coupling of terminal alkynes with 2,3-
allenols affording the stereo-defined 1,3-enynals or enyl
ketones with an exclusive E selectivity (Figure 1c), which are
a type of common unit in natural or bioactive products (Figure
1d).
7

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
As shown in Figure 3, terminal alkynols with different lengths
of carbon chain between the C−C triple bond and the hydroxy
group afforded the corresponding products (E)-3aa∼(E)-3ca
in decent yields, and the reaction is robust since no protection
is required for the free OH group. Different alkyl-substituted
terminal alkynes without the hydroxy group also worked to
afford (E)-3da and (E)-3ea. Even the highly strained
cyclopropyl group survived, affording (E)-3fa. Terminal
alkynes bearing various highly synthetically versatile functional
groups, such as chloro (1g), cyano (1h), and ester (1i), may
also be applied, affording (E)-3ga∼(E)-3ia. Even the reaction

CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed a conceptually new approach
for the enyne synthesis via a single rhodium-catalyzed cross-
coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with 2,3-allenols. This
protocol enables an efficient and highly selective preparation of
(E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals under a set of ambient conditions,
which could serve as platform molecules for the synthesis of
many other useful molecules due to the accommodation of a
wide array of highly reactive functional groups. The synthetic
potential of this methodology has been demonstrated via
derivatization of bio-active molecules, the efficient total
syntheses of isotaxifolial D, and the synthesis of dehydroaci-
tretin. A mechanism has been proposed for the observed highly
selective formation of (E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals. The use of a
base is not required since the terminal alkynylmetalation
proceeds readily under base-free conditions, and the catalyti-
cally active rhodium catalyst has been regenerated via aerobic
oxidation with the help of HOAc. The development of many
other types of such reactions with both types of readily
available terminal alkynes and allenes as the reactants for enyne
syntheses is highly expected and is being actively pursued in
our laboratory.

ABSTRACT: Herein, a rhodium-catalyzed highly chemo-, regio-, and
stereo-selective linear cross coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with
readily available 2,3-allenols aforded the synthetically and biologically
versatile 3-alkyn-2(E)-enones/enals. The reaction exhibits a perfect
match of the reactivities for these two classes of compounds since the
well-known self-reacting products of both reactants were not formed.
The reaction enjoys a wide substrate scope under ambient conditions.
Furthermore, the synthetic potentials have been demonstrated by
utilizing this reaction as a pivotal step: a very concise two-step total
synthesis of naturally occurring isotaxifolial D has been achieved; an
eficient synthesis of dehydroacitretin by applying this reaction two times
has also been executed. Through mechanistic studies including D-
labeling experiments, it is proposed that the reaction proceeded via

■ CONCLUSIONS

In summary, we have developed a conceptually new approach
for the enyne synthesis via a single rhodium-catalyzed cross-
coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with 2,3-allenols. This
protocol enables an eficient and highly selective preparation of
(E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals under a set of ambient conditions,
which could serve as platform molecules for the synthesis of
many other useful molecules due to the accommodation of a
wide array of highly reactive functional groups. The synthetic
potential of this methodology has been demonstrated via
derivatization of bio-active molecules, the eficient total
syntheses of isotaxifolial D, and the synthesis of dehydroaci
tretin. A mechanism has been proposed for the observed highly
selective formation of (E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals. The use of a
base is not required since the terminal alkynylmetalation
proceeds readily under base-free conditions, and the catalyti-
cally active rhodium catalyst has been regenerated via aerobic
oxidation with the help of HOAc. The development of many

other types of such reactions with both types of readily
available terminal alkynes and allenes as the reactants for enyne
syntheses is highly expected and is being actively pursued in
our laboratory.
